data.narrative:
Dragonfly Aerospace is a Series G stage company in Space & Aerospace founded by Bryan Dean, having raised $20M to date. The valuation universe includes 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers, though narrow peer filtering yielded insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage matches for reliable median benchmarking.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable lens. Using total capital raised ($20M) as a proxy for current embedded value ($41M), application of a typical Series G step-up multiplier of 1.25x yields $51M. Peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable: while 14 Space & Aerospace peers exist in the dataset, filtering for same-stage or adjacent-stage companies and similar valuation tiers returned fewer than three datapoints. Public-comp anchoring via the sector P/S median (24.6x across the 5 public tickers) cannot be applied without disclosed target revenue.

Analysis supports a valuation range of $44M to $59M, centered on $51M. This estimate rests on a single methodological pillar, introducing material uncertainty. Key dependencies include whether the $41M implied current value accurately reflects pre-money equity buildup, and whether private aerospace companies at Series G typically command 1.25x step-ups. Absent revenue data and tight private-peer clustering, direct market comparables remain elusive. Additional diligence on historical capital deployment efficiency and technical de-risking would strengthen conviction in any final valuation.
